newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower as rally fizzles out.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower as rally fizzles out.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed weak on Tuesday after trading higher as a short-lived rally fizzled out, traders said.

"We rallied on the export inspections news that the Chinese had 2.4 million bushels inspected," said one trader. "That started the short-covering rally but after that there was nothing else to rally on."

USDA on Tuesday reported 2.425 million bushels of wheat inspected for export to China in the week ended Aug. 29. That figure was higher than trade expectations and could indicate a renewed willingness for China to accept U.S. wheat.
Traders noted China had rejected several shipments of U.S. wheat this summer on suspicion it was contaminated with TCK smut.
Few buyers could be found after the rally and wheat drifted lower most of the afternoon, closing weak, traders said.
Wheat ended one to four cents per bushel lower with September down one at $4.66-1/2.
